title: OET: The Healthcare English Test Format
summary: OET's four sub-tests for healthcare professionals — two shared, two profession-specific — scored 0–500 with an A–E grade.

chunks.heading: English for healthcare, not academia
chunks.body: OET tests English in a **healthcare context** for **12 professions** (nursing, medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and more). It has **four sub-tests — Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking** — using real workplace materials, so the language is clinical and practical rather than academic.
chunks.realExample: Instead of an academic essay, you'll write a referral letter; instead of a general talk, you'll hear a patient consultation — the tasks mirror your actual job.
chunks.memoryHook: English for your clinic, not a classroom. Four sub-tests, healthcare all the way.

chunks.heading: Two shared, two profession-specific
chunks.body: **Listening and Reading are the same for everyone** — generic healthcare topics accessible across professions. **Writing and Speaking are profession-specific**: a nurse and a doctor get different scenarios and materials matched to their field.
chunks.realExample: In Speaking, a physiotherapist role-plays a physio scenario while a pharmacist role-plays a pharmacy one — the profession-specific tasks reflect your own practice.
chunks.memoryHook: Listening & Reading = shared. Writing & Speaking = built for YOUR profession.

chunks.heading: Scored 0–500 with an A–E grade
chunks.body: Each sub-test gets a **numerical score from 0 to 500 (in 10-point steps)** mapped to a **letter grade A to E**. There's **no single overall score** — regulators look at your **per-sub-test grades**, often requiring **Grade B (around 350)** in each.
chunks.realExample: A nursing council might require Grade B in all four sub-tests — so a strong Reading won't compensate for a Writing below B. Each skill must clear the bar on its own.
chunks.memoryHook: 0–500 + A–E per sub-test. No overall — usually you need Grade B in each.

chunks.heading: It's accepted for registration and visas
chunks.body: OET is accepted by **healthcare regulators and immigration authorities** in the UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand and elsewhere for **professional registration and visas**. Confirm the **exact grade** your regulator and visa route require before booking.
chunks.realExample: The same OET result may satisfy both your professional registration and a work visa — but the required grade can differ, so check both authorities' current requirements.
chunks.memoryHook: Used for healthcare registration + visas. Confirm the exact grade each authority wants.

recall.q: Who is the OET designed for?
recall.a: Healthcare professionals across 12 professions (nursing, medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and more).

recall.q: Which OET sub-tests are shared and which are profession-specific?
recall.a: Listening and Reading are the same for everyone; Writing and Speaking are specific to your profession.
Each sub-test gets a numerical score from 0 to 500 (in 10-point steps) mapped to a letter grade A–E — there's no single overall score.

recall.q: What grade do regulators often require?
recall.a: Grade B (around 350) in each sub-test, though the exact requirement varies by authority.
Professional registration and visas in healthcare in the UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand and other countries.
